attributes.expression: SET [gen_Value] = @PrmMaxRevaluationDate, where @PrmMaxRevaluationDate varchar(30) = CONVERT(varchar(10), MAX(dateadd(hh,3,gen_revaluationdate)), 103) FROM Gen_fundmain WHERE gen_existinfile = 1 AND gen_revaluationdate < cast(YEAR(GETDATE()) as nvarchar) + '/' + CAST(MONTH(GETDATE()) as nvarchar) + '/' + '1'. I.e. the latest revaluation date (+3 hours fixed shift, no DST handling) of fund mains present in the file, strictly before the first day of the current month (server date), formatted as style 103 'dd/mm/yyyy' text. If no fund main qualifies, MAX is NULL and gen_Value is set to NULL.

declaredSources.why: MAX(dateadd(hh,3,gen_revaluationdate)) converted to varchar(10) style 103 (dd/mm/yyyy) becomes gen_Value
only fund mains with gen_existinfile = 1 take part in the MAX

only revaluation dates < first day of the current month (string 'YYYY/M/1' built from GETDATE(), implicitly converted for the comparison) take part in the MAX; the filter uses the raw column, the +3h shift is applied only in the SELECT

Unsupported write: direct UPDATE on the CRM Base table gen_SystemConfigurationBase (bypasses CRM plugins/audit; ModifiedOn not set by the statement - general CRM behaviour, not provable from the package). The value is read from the CRM view Gen_fundmain (non-Base) in the same DB.

Date-string comparison (hypothesis, depends on session settings not in the package): the bound 'YYYY/M/1' is a string implicitly converted to the type of gen_revaluationdate. For datetime, SQL Server interprets slash-separated year-first strings according to the session DATEFORMAT (e.g. under dmy it may be read as year/day/month). With the default us_english (mdy) it is read as year/month/day. The login language of the SSIS account is external_unknown.

Time zone: gen_revaluationdate in the Gen_fundmain view is compared without the +3h shift but returned with dateadd(hh,3,...) (fixed +3, no DST). Whether the stored values are UTC is not provable from the package.
